TextBlock.Text: TIMOR SEA, late afternoon. Rig Seventeen stopped answering its shore office on Tuesday. Forty-one contract staff are still aboard, and the people holding the platform have a helicopter deck, a shore battery on the nearest headland and an air-defence vehicle they were not supposed to have. The coastal state has asked for help and set the boundary: you may cover an evacuation, you may not level the installation. CHOULES is in company with CANBERRA and there are two Super Stallions for the lift. Get the transports in, get the people off, get everybody out before the light goes. Not every platform out here is theirs and most of this coast is working its ordinary week.
Commodore Alex Mercer; Captain Ratna Prasetyo, TNI-AL, embarked

The platform is not a target. The people on its upper deck are Captain Prasetyo's problem afterwards and not yours now. Two airframes, one lift each, and a patrol closing from the north that has answered nobody. Get the crew off before it arrives, or hold it off until they are.
Evacuate: Get a lift helicopter clear to the south with the platform crew Platform: Leave the civilian platform standing Ships: Keep both amphibious ships afloat
HMAS Choules and HMAS Canberra with two CH-53E for the lift. Ashore: a launcher site, a VL MICA battery, a Sosna vehicle and a technical. One armed platform.
60 minutes. The operation ends when the clock runs out, and the main objective fails with it.
Destroying a neutral contact ends the operation in failure. Identify before you shoot.
